name: calendar
description: A month and what is on in it, at whatever size it has been given: a marker with a count, a short agenda, a month grid, or a full page with an action beside every event. To ask someone for a date use datepicker.

month.description: The month to show, as YYYY-MM, for example 2026-09.

detail.title: How much to show
detail.description: glance is a marker with how many things are coming, for a corner or a narrow pane. brief is the next few, as a list. full is the month grid. page is the month with an action beside every event, for when the calendar has the screen to itself. Expanding a block asks for page.

caption.description: Names the calendar. Defaults to the month and year.

events.description: What is on, each on one day. Days with nothing are left empty.

label.description: Short: what it is, not a description.

time.description: Optional time, shown before the label.

actions.description: Components placed inside this event, shown at page detail. Each is {component, props}: a button or a link, nothing that would trap someone inside a calendar cell.

today.description: A day to mark as today, as YYYY-MM-DD. Marked with text as well as colour.

upcoming.title: How many to list
upcoming.description: How many events glance counts and brief lists, from today onwards.

a11y.role: table at full and page detail, list at brief, status at glance

keyboard.does: focuses the scroll region when the month is wider than the space, and reaches each event's actions at page detail

wcag.notes: Every size is a real structure rather than a styled version of the same one: a status with a count, a list, or a table whose days are announced with their weekday column header (1.3.1). Day cells name their full date, so a day read out of context still says which day it is. Today is marked with the word today as well as a colour (1.4.1) and with aria-current. At glance the count is spoken in full, so a number in a circle is never the only way to know what it means.

a11y.notes: At full detail in a narrow container each event becomes a marker rather than a label: which days are busy is what a month that size can honestly answer, and the labels stay in the accessibility tree.

machine.identify: Read data-detail for which size is being shown and data-month for the month. At full and page detail each day cell carries data-date; at any detail each event carries data-event and data-date.
machine.operate: The calendar itself is not interactive. At page detail each event may carry its own buttons and links, which are operated like any other.
